lines.x: It's wise to care for your safety, Doctor. But you can work without worry now, I'll keep you protected.

I've met plenty who claim to practice martial arts. Most are posers who lack substance, not Waai Fu. She's an interesting one... although her training is not yet complete. I look forward to sparring with her, once she's ready.

Rhodes Island doesn't have a cellar, you say? Hmm… Now that won't do. Alcohol is indispensable. It's meant to be savored, enjoyed, and sometimes used to numb the pain. Trust me, Doctor, build a cellar. I know exactly what you'll need to stock it.

I built a library back in Mansfield. Most of the books I could get my hands on were Columbian, and thus, my extensive reading eventually brought a sense of monotony. It is most pleasing that Rhodes Island has such a diverse collection of books.

Schemes and ploys meant nothing in the face of absolute power... Or so I thought, until I realized that no power is truly absolute, at least not mine. Now, I never underestimate anything or anyone, no matter how insignificant they seem.

I used to think that Rhodes Island was just another Mansfield, a 'free' prison. And you, just another me—a convict unchained, a king behind bars. But now I see that I was mistaken. This is not a prison, and you, Doctor, are a friend to all.

Are the ones over there from Rhine Lab? Don't worry. I bear no grudge against Rhine Lab itself, and I won't harm them in anyway. Farce like that will only complicate things for you, Doctor. However, one of these days, I might need to ask them about one thing.
Doctor, are you free later? Let me take you out for a drink. Nothing important. I merely have a few secrets that I'd like to get off my chest. You are the first new friend I've made in a long time.
You are a very good friend, Doctor. If I manage to survive after sorting everything out, do come visit me at Mansfield. That's my kingdom, and what is mine there is also yours.
Falling asleep so trustingly in the company of others... Is that really trust, or have you slipped up?

I owe Rhodes Island my life, and so my candor must befit the weight of my debt, Doctor. I am going after a certain department within Rhine Lab. If you don't want your relationship with them ruined, now is the time to turn me away.
Battlefield experience... Indeed, that's something that I lack. Much obliged, Doctor.
Doctor, do not be afraid. The fury of my fist will not fall upon the undeserving.

Look well, Doctor. My composure, politeness, and grace are but a mask. Peel that off, and you'll find me at my truest, bloodthirsty, violent, and destructive. See me, know me... only then be my friend.
Perfect time to get a pump.
Listen to your leader, me.
Let's go.
Never underestimate the enemy.
At your call.
Where to?
I'll remember to dial it back.
I won't let them go any further.
Face me!
Is that all? Strike me like your lives depend on it!
Come on, bring it on!
Warm-up's over!
True grit must be tested in adversity, but we must be careful not to punch above our weight.
Good boxers never show all their tricks unless needed. Operations are the same, Doctor.
Violence without just cause is but mindless abuse. I've learnt to rein in my urges long ago.
As long as we're still alive, we're not defeated.
Pardon me, but the ceiling in Rhodes Island is a little low…
Oh?
Doctor, have you read any good books recently? I have a few to recommend.
Arknights.

New Year's hasn't meant much to me for a long, long time. You see, prisoners don't usually hope much for tomorrow, or the future. But now that I'm a part of Rhodes Island, I suppose I should try to change that. Happy New Year, Doctor.
Stay vigilant, Doctor.

Doctor, happy birthday. It shames me to admit that if I were still in Mansfield, or earlier in Columbia, I would have arranged a far grander celebration for you. Now, the best I can offer is a well-prepared drink. Would you do me the honor?

What a lively day. You could say that Oripathy is like a shackle on life itself, depriving people of their freedom and their futures. Yet even in the confined space of Rhodes Island, I still see hope in the eyes of many. This has given me no small revelation on my own future.
